import numpy as np


def pca(x, components, *, method="svd"):
    """Center data and return transformed rows, principal axes, variance, and mean.

    Axes are rows, sorted by decreasing variance. Signs are conventional and can
    differ between methods; compare subspaces/reconstructions rather than signs.
    """
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    if x.ndim != 2 or len(x) < 2 or not 1 <= components <= min(x.shape):
        raise ValueError("invalid PCA dimensions")
    mean = x.mean(0)
    centered = x - mean
    if method == "svd":
        _, singular, axes = np.linalg.svd(centered, full_matrices=False)
        variance = singular**2 / (len(x) - 1)
    elif method == "eigh":
        variance, vectors = np.linalg.eigh(centered.T @ centered / (len(x) - 1))
        order = np.argsort(variance)[::-1]
        axes, variance = vectors[:, order].T, np.maximum(variance[order], 0)
    else:
        raise ValueError("method must be svd or eigh")
    axes = axes[:components]
    return centered @ axes.T, axes, variance[:components], mean

Center features before PCA. Eigenvectors of the sample covariance and right singular vectors of the centered matrix span the same principal subspace; eigenvalues equal singular_values²/(N−1). SVD avoids forming a covariance matrix whose condition number is squared. Eigenvector signs and bases inside repeated-eigenvalue subspaces are not unique, so compare reconstructions or projectors.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For centered $X=U\Sigma V^T$, principal axes are columns of $V$ and explained variances are $\sigma_j^2/(N-1)$. Rank-k reconstruction $U_k\Sigma_kV_k^T$ minimizes squared reconstruction error among rank-k matrices. Scaling columns changes the objective, so covariance PCA and standardized/correlation PCA answer different questions. [3](https://www.statlearning.com/)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://jakevdp.github.io/PythonDataScienceHandbook/05.09-principal-component-analysis.html) and [2](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/decomposition.html).
